translations.idiomatic: On that summer day in 274 Jin’s Empress Yang Yan passed—alas!

sentences.zh: 昔有莘適殷，姜姒歸周，宣德中闈，徽音永流。

translations.literal: Ancient Youxin married Yin; Jiang Si returned to Zhou—virtue spread within the palace, fair fame forever flows.
translations.idiomatic: Youxin wed Yin; Jiang water wed Zhou—inner chambers rang with virtue.

translations.literal: The two Ji ladies of Fan and Wei steadied Qi and aided Chu;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ji and Wei Ji uplifted Qi and Chu;

translations.literal: the two consorts Ma and Deng likewise aided Han sovereigns.
translations.idiomatic: Ma and Deng consorts beside Han sovereigns did the same.

translations.literal: Lofty primal queen—you glorified consorts of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Towering primal queen—you lit the Jin harem.

translations.literal: You matched the sage emperor—tracks aligned with ancient models.
translations.idiomatic: You walked beside the sage throne as queens of old.

translations.literal: Heaven granted no long span—you turned from yang toward shade.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven refused long life—you crossed from light to shade.

translations.literal: Six palaces wailed; four seas shared torn hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Six wings of the harem keened; all beneath Heaven tore their breasts.

translations.literal: Alas, mean concubine—I bore uniquely deep grace.
translations.idiomatic: Mean concubine though I am—your kindness pierced deepest.

translations.literal: I chase the Three Worthies—gladly I would sink myself.
translations.idiomatic: I envy the three who followed Duke Mu—I would gladly sink with you.

translations.literal: What use is longing?
translations.idiomatic: Why hoard longing?

translations.literal: Never forget virtuous words.
translations.idiomatic: Keep your virtuous words alive.

translations.literal: What use is chronicling?
translations.idiomatic: Why record deeds?

translations.literal: Entrust phrases to the brush grove.
translations.idiomatic: Commit them to ink and Hanlin.

translations.literal: Thus she composed the dirge, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Thus runs her lament:

translations.literal: Radiant primal queen—you sprang from Yang.
translations.idiomatic: Bright primal queen—you rose from the house of Yang.

translations.literal: For generations vermillion wheels gleamed—Huayang blazed.
translations.idiomatic: Generation on generation rode vermillion wheels—Huayang blazed.

translations.literal: The peak sent down spirits—revealing these auspicious signs.
translations.idiomatic: Sacred peaks poured forth spirit—showing these blessed omens.

translations.literal: Earnestly was born a splendid maid—she bore radiant glory.
translations.idiomatic: From them sprang a heroine blazing with light.

translations.literal: She housed spirit and grasped pattern—unlike common Jiang brides.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit and letters dwelt in her—not common flesh.

translations.literal: Gentle as spring sun; carriage stern as autumn frost.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle as vernal sun; resolve sharp as autumn frost.

translations.literal: She hated those who rushed heedlessly; she cherished righteous rule.
translations.idiomatic: She spurned reckless ease and upheld righteous paths.

translations.literal: She followed the four teachings—never slack, never waste.
translations.idiomatic: She walked the four teachings—never idle, never wild.

translations.literal: She moved through six kinships—fair fame rose bright.
translations.idiomatic: Among six degrees of kin her sweet fame rang.

translations.literal: Where did that fame shine?
translations.idiomatic: Where did her praise ring?

translations.literal: The capital chamber held her good.
translations.idiomatic: It rang through the royal house.

translations.literal: Betrothed and welcomed—she married the sage emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Courtship led her to the sage sovereign’s side.

translations.literal: She rectified inner thresholds—virtue led her charge.
translations.idiomatic: She ordered inner gates—virtue guided every step.

translations.literal: Jade pendants sounded with measure; speech carried patterned grace.
translations.idiomatic: Her pendants chimed in rhythm; every phrase wore pattern.

translations.literal: She looked up to illustrated charts; bent to scan texts.
translations.idiomatic: She studied charts above and rolled texts below.

translations.literal: She consulted female scribes; asked counsel of bamboo and silk.
translations.idiomatic: She queried palace scholars and silk-bound histories.

translations.literal: She sought to charm royal mother-in-law—dawn and dusk reverent.
translations.idiomatic: She charmed her royal mother-in-law with dawn-and-dusk reverence.

translations.literal: She truly ordered inner kitchens—each task performed with awe.
translations.idiomatic: She governed inner kitchens—every duty performed with awe.

translations.literal: In ritual she toiled; in reverence she strove.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual bent her back; reverence drove her nights.

translations.literal: Although called peerlessly holy, her virtue renewed daily.
translations.idiomatic: Though hailed unequaled, her virtue renewed each dawn.

translations.literal: What meant daily renewal?
translations.idiomatic: What did renewal bring?

translations.literal: She widened lavish kindness—she cherished the emperor’s sisters.
translations.idiomatic: Ever-kind, ever-gentle—she cherished the emperor’s own sisters.

translations.literal: She wove order through six palaces—nothing escaped her net.
translations.idiomatic: She threaded six wings of the harem—nothing slipped her weave.

translations.literal: Concubines looked up as to the pole star.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser ladies looked up as to the North Star.

translations.literal: Already green spring—the turtle dove announces season.
translations.idiomatic: Spring greens when turtle-doves call the hour.

translations.literal: She grasped mulberry hooks herself—leading attendant brides.
translations.idiomatic: She led brides with mulberry hook in hand.

translations.literal: She finished silkworm trays—partitioned cocoons, sorted silk.
translations.idiomatic: She tended trays, split cocoons, sorted filament.

translations.literal: She inspected women’s work—she directed ritual robes.
translations.idiomatic: She inspected needlework and fashioned sacral gowns.

translations.literal: She reverently served the ancestral temple—ever speaking filial thought.
translations.idiomatic: She served the temple—always mindful of filial hearts.

translations.literal: Of those six conducts—she trod every one.
translations.idiomatic: She practiced every womanly virtue.

translations.literal: Huang and Ying aided Shun; Tushan winged Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Ehuang and Nüying aided Shun; Tushan aided Yu.

translations.literal: Only Wei, only Fan—two hegemons relied on them.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Ji and Fan Ji steadied two hegemons.

translations.literal: Bright bright our queen—different age, same square rule.
translations.idiomatic: Bright our queen—another age, same measure.

translations.literal: She too could cope with turmoil [4]; she planned with Heaven’s treasury.
translations.idiomatic: She too could heal unrest [4]; she schemed with Heaven’s storehouse.

translations.literal: Within she spread women’s teaching; without she aided yang transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Within she spread yin teaching; without she aided yang rule.

translations.literal: She bound together myriad officers—diligent night and day.
translations.idiomatic: She knit every minister—tireless day and night.

translations.literal: Grace rode the wind; bounty fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Her grace rode wind; her bounty fell like rain.

translations.literal: Inner and outer gained bliss—near and far sang praise.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside flourished; near and far sang hymns.

translations.literal: Heaven’s mandate stayed auspicious—multiplying, branching wide.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven kept auspicious fate—family branches multiplied.

translations.literal: Thus came hundredfold blessing—bearing sages and worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Blessings arrived in hundreds—bearing sage sons and worthy princes.

translations.literal: Teaching surpassed Ren and Si; instruction overtook Jiang Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Her teaching topped Si and Ren; her norms surpassed Jiang Yuan.

translations.literal: Grand stands the crown prince—root of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty the heir—pillar of the realm.

translations.literal: Splendid princes of Nanyang—screens and hedges for the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Splendid Nanyang princes—screens and river guards.

translations.literal: Root and branch shade thick—four seas rest beneath.
translations.idiomatic: Root and branch spread shade—the realm rests cool.

translations.literal: Without this royal mother—who could reach such zenith?
translations.idiomatic: Without this queen mother—who could climb so high?

translations.literal: They say Qian is keen; they say sage is true.
translations.idiomatic: They call Heaven keen; they call sageness true.

translations.literal: Hall piled with goodness—five blessings assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Goodness piled high—the five blessings gather.

translations.literal: She should enjoy lofty years—not fall, not tilt.
translations.idiomatic: She deserved long years—never to fall or fail.

translations.literal: Like Peng’s tooth-count; like Dan’s lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: Like Peng Zu’s span; like Laozi’s age.

translations.literal: Why was fortune not granted—here calamity struck [5]?
translations.idiomatic: Why deny Heaven’s favor—why strike her here [5]?

translations.literal: Illness lingered at death’s gate—sleep brought no peace.
translations.idiomatic: She lingered at death’s door—no sleep brought ease.

translations.literal: Wu Xian wielded arts; He and Bian offered prescriptions.
translations.idiomatic: Shaman Wu worked spells; healers He and Que brewed drafts.

translations.literal: Prayers won no answer; tasted drugs brought no cure.
translations.idiomatic: Prayers failed; every draught proved vain.

translations.literal: Body and spirit parted—darkening, wasting.
translations.idiomatic: Body and soul slipped apart—dimming into gloom.

translations.literal: Suddenly she collapsed—spirit sank, light died.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly she fell—light drowned in dark.

translations.literal: Mournful crown prince—Nanyang’s flowering prince.
translations.idiomatic: The heir mourns—the flourishing prince of Nanyang.

translations.literal: He climbs yet cannot sleep—beats breast and breast is torn.
translations.idiomatic: He cannot climb from grief—beats his breast till bones break.

translations.literal: Alas, oh grief!
translations.idiomatic: Alas for this sorrow!

translations.literal: Whole palace wailed—the realm within seas trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Every hall keened—the realm inside the seas shook.

translations.literal: Runners choked the avenues—mourners jammed the courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Runners clogged roads—mourners packed the yard.

translations.literal: Grief crashed like thunder—tears fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning crashed like thunder; tears fell like showers.

translations.literal: Sobs cease not—as if parents were lost.
translations.idiomatic: No sob ends—as if a parent died.

translations.literal: Emperor and consort—long joined in ancient pledge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor and queen—pledged long ago.

translations.literal: Wing to wing from white-thatched halls—paired flight to purple towers.
translations.idiomatic: They nested in humble roofs—then flew paired to purple halls.

translations.literal: Mourning queen, wounded queen—early she entered the vault.
translations.idiomatic: They mourn their queen—she sank too soon to stone.

translations.literal: Words reach here—tears and mucus fall.
translations.idiomatic: Speech stops here—tears and mucus fall.

translations.literal: Tracing my queen—truly keen, truly wise.
translations.idiomatic: Remembering her—truly keen, truly wise.

translations.literal: She penetrated nature and fate—she grasped thrift’s rule.
translations.idiomatic: She grasped life’s truth—she mastered austerity.

translations.literal: Funeral rites matched plain antiquity—pared like highest ages.
translations.idiomatic: Her burial honored utmost thrift—plain as oldest times.

translations.literal: Burial garments held no treasure; mouth jewels held no bright moon-pearl.
translations.idiomatic: Her grave clothes bore no gems; no pearl filled her mouth.

translations.literal: Hidden radiance in the catalpa palace—forever turned from clear light.
translations.idiomatic: Her gleam sinks in the catalpa bier—gone from daylight forever.

translations.literal: Concubines and maids wail—together cut off.
translations.idiomatic: We servants keened—we shared that rupture.

translations.literal: Courtyard silence grows dense—dark chambers deepen shade.
translations.idiomatic: Courtyards fell mute; shadow thickened every room.

translations.literal: Canopies stand empty—robes and quilts vainly spread.
translations.idiomatic: Silken curtains hang hollow; quilts lie unused.

translations.literal: Men also say the spirit path cannot be traced.
translations.idiomatic: Men say ghost roads cannot be traced.

translations.literal: Far drifts her shining soul—does it float or sink?
translations.idiomatic: Her bright soul wanders—does it rise or sink?

translations.literal: Rich offerings daily spread—we hope the soul draws near.
translations.idiomatic: Opulent gifts pile daily—we pray her ghost approaches.

translations.literal: Who says the primal queen—cannot hear her voice?
translations.idiomatic: Who claims our primal queen hears nothing now?

translations.literal: Thus they debated her lofty course—her course already overflowed [6].
translations.idiomatic: They praised her conduct—it already overflowed measure [6].

translations.literal: Thus they consulted tortoise and milfoil—both auguries doubled auspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Tortoise and yarrow both answered doubly auspicious.

translations.literal: Therefore they fixed tomb precinct—completed the dark chamber.
translations.idiomatic: They fixed the grave site—raised the hidden vault.

translations.literal: The soul journeys hence—on this appointed day.
translations.idiomatic: Her soul sets forth—this chosen day.

translations.literal: Morning of mid-autumn—Venus first rises.
translations.idiomatic: Autumn dawn—morning star climbs.

translations.literal: Stars arrayed, harness at dawn—spirit carriage teams four bays.
translations.idiomatic: Stars still blaze as horses hitch—the spirit coach spans four bays.

translations.literal: What was her carriage?
translations.idiomatic: What coach bore her?

translations.literal: Golden root and jade chest.
translations.idiomatic: Gold-wheeled coach and jade-lined chest.

translations.literal: What were her bays?
translations.idiomatic: What bays drew her?

translations.literal: Twin white foals and paired yellow steeds.
translations.idiomatic: White Luos paired with golden bays.

translations.literal: Rustling draped coach—vermillion robes and cinnabar seal-pattern.
translations.idiomatic: Rustling draped bier—scarlet robes and vermillion stripes.

translations.literal: Dim hearse wagons—mourning caps and sackcloth skirts.
translations.idiomatic: Low rumbling hearses—mourning bands and hemp skirts.

translations.literal: Splendid hubs blaze the wilds—white canopies mantle the plain.
translations.idiomatic: Jeweled hubs flame across fields—white shades blanket the moor.

translations.literal: Exorcist-mask bearers stride—pennons and ghost-flags whirl.
translations.idiomatic: Masked squaremen march—spirit banners whip and flutter.

translations.literal: Dirge boys lead songs—white horses cry at traces.
translations.idiomatic: Children guide laments—white steeds keen at shafts.

translations.literal: Spectators crowd the road—gentlemen and ladies weep streams.
translations.idiomatic: Roadways jam with watchers—lords and ladies sob.

translations.literal: Thousand carriages, myriad riders—reach those steep hills.
translations.idiomatic: Thousands of riders climb toward steep Jun ridge.

translations.literal: Jun ridge towers—layered peaks fold ridge on ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Jun summit rises—ridge folds on ridge.

translations.literal: Vast height and open breadth—it fronts Luo with Yellow River at its back.
translations.idiomatic: Lofty and bright—it faces Luo with River behind.

translations.literal: Left gaze royal mother-in-law—right glance imperial kin.
translations.idiomatic: Left toward royal mothers—right toward imperial tombs.

translations.literal: Measuring life and death—bright spirits approve.
translations.idiomatic: Judging life and death—the gods approve.

translations.literal: Aunts and sisters, wives and cousins, brides and attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Aunts, sisters, co-wives, and maids—

translations.literal: They chased dust of wheel-tracks—wailing clogged roadways.
translations.idiomatic: they chased the dust—wailing choked every lane.

translations.literal: Princes and nobles—gathered like clouds, scattered like stars.
translations.idiomatic: Lords and ministers clustered like clouds and stars.

translations.literal: Hosts of officers—white canopies beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Official multitudes—countless white shades.

translations.literal: Sighing through the night—east turns toward dawn.
translations.idiomatic: They sighed till dawn broke east.

translations.literal: Hundred gods attend—our queen finds rest.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits greet her—our queen is laid to rest.

translations.literal: Inner and outer stand vigil—shared grief and longing.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside mourn together.

translations.literal: Tears like linked clouds—drops like heavy dew.
translations.idiomatic: Tears hang like clouds—drops fall like dew.

translations.literal: Gate leaves shut tight—deep dark within.
translations.idiomatic: Stone gates sealed—depths sink black.

translations.literal: Night without day—what use is light?
translations.idiomatic: Night without sun—what good is sight?

translations.literal: No mound raised, no tree planted—hill slopes keep plain shape.
translations.idiomatic: No mound, no marker—she lies plain as the slope.

translations.literal: When former queen died—great Fire constellation sank west.
translations.idiomatic: When she died last year—the Fire star slid west.

translations.literal: Cold went, heat passed—again we reach first autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Cold yielded to heat—again first autumn comes.

translations.literal: Since I bore grief—a blur one full cycle.
translations.idiomatic: Since grief seized me—a year flashed past.

translations.literal: Garments soon change—pain grips like twisting entrails.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning clothes turn—my vitals twist.

translations.literal: Forced by ritual codes—only grief increases.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual presses harder—only sorrow swells.

translations.literal: Leaving these plain robes—I cling to spirit hill.
translations.idiomatic: I shed white hemp yet cling to her burial mound.

translations.literal: Having beginning and end—is Heaven and Earth’s warp.
translations.idiomatic: Beginnings and endings weave Heaven’s law.

translations.literal: Unless you are three luminaries—who avoids decay?
translations.idiomatic: Unless you are sun, moon, stars—who escapes falling?

translations.literal: Living she spread fair virtue—dead her image paints silks.
translations.idiomatic: Alive she spread virtue—dead artists paint her face.

translations.literal: Former sages held this—their glory.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient worthies deemed this their glory.

translations.literal: Gentle primal queen—she truly spread kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle primal queen—she widowed kindness.

translations.literal: She nurtured all creatures—grace welled forth.
translations.idiomatic: She nurtured every life—kindness overflowed.

translations.literal: Love left behind never ends—forever remembered.
translations.idiomatic: Her love lingers—memory never fades.

translations.literal: Her name hangs with sun and moon—through myriad springs.
translations.idiomatic: Her name rides moon and sun—through endless springs.

translations.literal: Alas mean concubine—I feel the four seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Mean concubine feels—four seasons turn.

translations.literal: Speaking longing, speaking yearning—tears trail down.
translations.idiomatic: Each word of longing—tears trail.

sentences.zh: 咸寧二年，納悼后，芬于座受詔作頌，其辭曰：

translations.literal: In second Xianning they brought in Empress Dao; Fen at seat received edict to compose praise, saying:
translations.idiomatic: In 276 they welcomed Empress Yang Zhi; Zuo Fen took orders at banquet to hymn her:

translations.literal: Towering Mount Hua—crest piercing pure heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Towering Huashan—summit kisses sky.

translations.literal: Giant Spirit cleaves currents—the Yellow River follows its course.
translations.idiomatic: River Lord splits torrents—the Great River keeps its channel.

translations.literal: Spirit of the river—spirit of the peak.
translations.idiomatic: Spirit of ford and spirit of peak—

translations.literal: They chimed on Yang clan—bearing this splendid brightness.
translations.idiomatic: —they fused in House Yang and bred this brilliance.

translations.literal: Solemn our queen—she answered fate and rose supreme.
translations.idiomatic: August queen—born to meet the hour.

translations.literal: She bore keen wit and trod wisdom—child prodigy early formed.
translations.idiomatic: Clever from birth—child sage mature.

translations.literal: Like orchid lush—like jade lustrous.
translations.idiomatic: Orchid lush—jade radiant.

translations.literal: Though still in cradle—she bore fair fame.
translations.idiomatic: Still in swaddling—already famed.

translations.literal: Her fame flew eight poles—she gathered praise in purple court.
translations.idiomatic: Her voice crossed eight zones—purple palace applauded.

translations.literal: Beyond Ren and Si—her virtue pairs Huang and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Past Ren and Si—she rivals Ehuang and Nüying.

translations.literal: Capital praised her—full rites performed betrothal.
translations.idiomatic: The court esteemed her—honored matchmakers sealed the pact.

translations.literal: Bright month, lucky day—hundred officers welcomed her.
translations.idiomatic: On chosen moon and day—every minister welcomed her.

translations.literal: Zhou-sheng returned to Han—the poets sing.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou-sheng wed Han—the poets sang.

translations.literal: Our queen arrived—carriages and robes gleamed.
translations.idiomatic: Our queen arrived—coach lacquer flashed.

translations.literal: She mounted Polar Throne—bright virtue daily waxed.
translations.idiomatic: She mounted throne—virtue brightened daily.

translations.literal: All folk rejoiced—all within seas shared joy.
translations.idiomatic: All lands rejoiced—the realm within seas sang.

translations.literal: Solemn sage emperor—profound wisdom utterly pure.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn sage emperor—pure in deepest wit.

translations.literal: He pitied cruel turmoil—spread kindness and planted mercy.
translations.idiomatic: He pitied cruel times—spread mercy everywhere.

translations.literal: He wiped stains and washed filth—renewed with seasons.
translations.idiomatic: He washed sin away—made all things new.

translations.literal: Surging great amnesty—edicts shook distant shores.
translations.idiomatic: Grand amnesty rolled—edicts shook frontiers.

translations.literal: When she mounted throne—prisons stood empty.
translations.idiomatic: When she rose—jails gaped empty.

translations.literal: Ten thousand lands rejoiced—six zones shared delight.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand states danced—six directions sang.

translations.literal: Earth goddess claps—Heaven and man rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Earth spirit dances—Heaven and mortals thrill.

translations.literal: Omens rise—sun and moon display essence.
translations.idiomatic: Good omens arrive—sun and moon blaze essence.

translations.literal: Harmony veils warm mist—three luminaries blaze clear.
translations.idiomatic: Warm vapors coil—three lights burn bright.

translations.literal: Season blessed—they soon spread sweet snow.
translations.idiomatic: Blessed hour brings timely snow.

translations.literal: Dark clouds veil thick—numinous dew drifts fine.
translations.idiomatic: Purple clouds billow—spirit dew drifts.

translations.literal: Stored and piled—it waits for sun to dry.
translations.idiomatic: Moisture gathers—sun must dry it.

translations.literal: Moisture soaks—soft rains central fields.
translations.idiomatic: Warm vapor drenches—capital fields soften.

translations.literal: Long enjoy rich years—blessing and wage forever calm.
translations.idiomatic: Enjoy fat harvests—wealth and peace endure.

sentences.zh: 及帝女萬年公主薨，帝痛悼不已，詔芬為誄，其文甚麗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu’s daughter Princess Wannian died, the emperor grieved endlessly and ordered Fen to compose a dirge—its prose extremely beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Wannian died Wu mourned without cease and bid Zuo Fen write—her elegy was splendid.

sentences.zh: 帝重芬詞藻，每有方物異寶，必詔為賦頌，以是屢獲恩賜焉。

translations.literal: The emperor prized Fen’s phrasing; whenever rare treasures arrived he ordered rhapsodies and hymns—thereby she repeatedly received imperial gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He prized her lines; each tribute beast or gem won an ode—she gathered repeated gifts.

sentences.zh: 答兄思詩、書及雜賦頌數十篇，並行于世。

translations.literal: Replies to brother Si’s poems, letters, and assorted rhapsodies and hymns—several tens of pieces—all circulated in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Her replies to Zuo Si and dozens of essays circulated widely.

translations.literal: Honorable Lady Hu
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hu of Honorable Rank

translations.literal: Honorable Lady Hu was named Fang.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Hu Fang bore that name.

translations.literal: Her father Fen has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Hu Fen has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 泰始九年，帝多簡良家子女以充內職，自擇其美者以絳紗繫臂。

translations.literal: In ninth Taishi year the emperor broadly drafted daughters of good houses for inner service and personally tied crimson gauze on those he deemed fairest.
translations.idiomatic: In 273 he drafted palace girls from good families and marked his favorites with crimson silk arm-bands.

translations.literal: When Fang entered selection she descended the hall weeping and crying.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fang crossed the hall weeping once chosen.

translations.literal: Attendants beside her stopped her: “His Majesty will hear your voice.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants hissed, “The emperor will hear.

translations.literal: ” Fang said: “I fear not death—why fear His Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: ” She shot back, “I fear death itself—why fear an emperor?”

sentences.zh: 」帝遣洛陽令司馬肇策拜芳為貴嬪。

translations.literal: ” The emperor ordered Luoyang Magistrate Sima Zhao to invest Fang as honorable lady by tally.
translations.idiomatic: ” Emperor Wu had Luoyang prefect Sima Zhao invest her with honorable rank.

sentences.zh: 帝每有顧問，不飾言辭，率爾而答，進退方雅。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor questioned her she did not polish phrases—answered plainly yet withdrew with modest grace.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he questioned her she answered straight without flourish—yet comported herself with modest grace.

sentences.zh: 時帝多內寵，平吳之後復納孫皓宮人數千，自此掖庭殆將萬人。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor greatly favored inner chambers; after conquering Wu he took several thousand of Sun Hao’s palace women—thereafter pepper chambers neared ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: After Wu fell he absorbed thousands of Sun Hao’s girls until the harem neared ten thousand souls.

sentences.zh: 而並寵者甚眾，帝莫知所適，常乘羊車，恣其所之，至便宴寢。

translations.literal: Many equally favored—emperor knew not whom to choose—often rode goat-drawn cart wherever it pleased, feasting and bedding where it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: So many favorites he rode a goat cart wherever chance led and slept there.

sentences.zh: 宮人乃取竹葉插戶，以鹽汁灑地，而引帝車。

translations.literal: Palace ladies therefore inserted bamboo leaves in doors, sprinkled salt water on ground to lure emperor’s cart.
translations.idiomatic: Women sprinkled salt and hung bamboo leaves to steer his goat cart.

sentences.zh: 然芳最蒙愛幸，殆有專房之寵焉，侍御服飾亞于皇后。

translations.literal: Yet Fang received deepest favor—almost exclusive chamber privilege—attendants’ robes secondary only to empress.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Fang won nearest monopoly favor—her wardrobe rivaled the empress.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與之摴蒱，爭矢，遂傷上指。

translations.literal: Emperor once played chupu with her; quarreling over arrows they wounded his finger.
translations.idiomatic: Playing dice for arrows she wounded his finger.

translations.literal: Emperor angrily said: “This truly is general stock!
translations.idiomatic: He snapped, “That’s pure warrior blood!

sentences.zh: 」芳對曰：「北伐公孫，西距諸葛，非將種而何？

translations.literal: ” Fang replied: “North you attacked Gongsun—west you resisted Zhuge—if not general stock, what?
translations.idiomatic: ” She shot back, “You marched north against Gongsun and west against Zhuge—what else is warlord stock?”

translations.literal: ” The emperor felt deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: He flushed with shame.

translations.literal: Fang bore Princess Wu’an.
translations.idiomatic: She bore Princess Wu’an.

translations.literal: Lady Zhuge
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhuge

sentences.zh: 諸葛夫人名婉，琅邪陽都人也。

translations.literal: Lady Zhuge was named Wan, a native of Yangdu in Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhuge Wan came from Yangdu in Langya.

translations.literal: Her father Chong, courtesy Maochang, was Commandant of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Zhuge Chong, courtesy Maochang, served as Commandant of Justice.

sentences.zh: 婉以泰始九年春入宮，帝臨軒，使使持節、洛陽令司馬肇拜為夫人。

translations.literal: In spring of ninth Taishi year she entered palace; emperor faced southern porch and ordered envoy with tally Luoyang Magistrate Sima Zhao to invest her as lady.
translations.idiomatic: In spring 273 she entered court; Emperor Wu had Sima Zhao invest her as Lady from the southern gallery.

translations.literal: Elder brother Quan, courtesy Delin, was Palace Rider Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Her brother Zhuge Quan, courtesy Delin, was a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 銓弟玫，字仁林，侍中、御史中丞。

translations.literal: Quan’s younger brother Mei, courtesy Renlin, was Palace Attendant and Palace Assistant Imperial Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Mei served as attendant and censor chief.

sentences.zh: 玫婦弟周穆，清河王覃之舅也。

translations.literal: Mei’s brother-in-law Zhou Mu was maternal uncle of Prince Qinghe of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Mei’s brother-in-law Zhou Mu was uncle to Prince Tan of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 永嘉初，穆與玫勸東海王越廢懷帝，立覃，越不許。

translations.literal: Early Yongjia, Mu with Mei urged Prince Donghai Yue to depose Emperor Huai and enthrone Tan—Yue refused.
translations.idiomatic: In early Yongjia Zhou Mu and Zhuge Mei urged Sima Yue to replace Huai with Tan—Yue refused.

sentences.zh: 重言之，越怒，遂斬玫及穆。

translations.literal: Urged again, Yue grew angry and executed Mei and Mu.
translations.idiomatic: When pressed again Yue beheaded both.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，玫謂穆曰：「我語卿何道？

translations.literal: Facing execution Mei said to Mu: “What did I tell you?
translations.idiomatic: Mei asked Zhou Mu, “Did I not warn you?”

translations.literal: ” Mu said: “What more is there to say today?
translations.idiomatic: Mu answered, “Nothing left to say.”

sentences.zh: 」時人方知謀出於穆，非玫之意。

translations.literal: ” People then learned the plot came from Mu—not Mei’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did folk realize Zhou Mu schemed it—not Mei.

translations.literal: Empress Jia of Emperor Hui
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia of Emperor Hui

sentences.zh: 惠賈皇后諱南風，平陽人也，小名時。

translations.literal: Empress Jia of Hui, taboo Nanfeng, native of Pingyang, childhood name Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia Nanfeng of Pingyang—pet name Shi.

translations.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 初，武帝欲為太子取衛瓘女，元后納賈郭親黨之說，欲婚賈氏。

translations.literal: At first Emperor Wu wished crown prince to marry Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yuan listened to Jia and Guo faction urging marriage with Jia clan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu favored Wei Guan’s daughter; Empress Yang Yan pushed Jia kin.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「衛公女有五可，賈公女有五不可。

translations.literal: Emperor said: “Lord Wei’s daughter has five goods—Lord Jia’s daughter five bads.
translations.idiomatic: Wu said, “Wei’s girl scores five merits—Jia’s five flaws.

sentences.zh: 衛家種賢而多子，美而長白；

translations.literal: Wei house breeds wise and many sons—beautiful, tall, fair;
translations.idiomatic: Weis are fertile and wise—fair and statuesque;

sentences.zh: 賈家種妒而少子，醜而短黑。

translations.literal: Jia house breeds jealousy and few sons—ugly, short, dark.
translations.idiomatic: Jias are jealous and barren—dark and squat.

sentences.zh: 」元后固請，荀顗、荀勖並稱充女之賢，乃定婚。

translations.literal: ” Empress Yuan pressed firmly—Xun Yi and Xun Xu together praised Chong’s daughter’s virtue—betrothal fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yan insisted; Xun Yi and Xun Xu praised Jia’s girl—the match closed.

sentences.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。

translations.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.
translations.idiomatic: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.

sentences.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。

translations.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.

sentences.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。

translations.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao in early 272 she became crown princess [7].

sentences.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。

translations.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.

sentences.zh: 帝常疑太子不慧，且朝臣和嶠等多以為言，故欲試之。

translations.literal: Emperor often suspected crown prince dull—and ministers such as He Qiao said same—so wished to test him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu doubted the heir’s wit—He Qiao agreed—so he tested him.

sentences.zh: 盡召東宮大小官屬，為設宴會，而密封疑事，使太子決之，停信待反。

translations.literal: He summoned all eastern palace officials large and small, set banquet, sealed doubtful affairs ordering crown prince to decide—stopped courier awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted Eastern Palace staff, sealed riddling cases for the heir to solve.

translations.literal: Consort greatly frightened—begged outsider compose answers.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jia panicked and outsourced answers.

translations.literal: Answerers mostly cited classical meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Ghostwriters packed classics.

translations.literal: Orderly Zhang Hong said: “Crown prince does not study.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Zhang Hong warned, “He never studied.

sentences.zh: 而答詔引義，必責作草主，更益譴負。

translations.literal: Yet reply edict cites meanings—surely will blame draft master—increasing blame.
translations.idiomatic: Classic prose exposes the ghostwriter.

translations.literal: Better answer straight from plain intent.
translations.idiomatic: Plain speech fits better.

sentences.zh: 」妃大喜，語泓：「便為我好答，富貴與汝共之。

translations.literal: ” Consort rejoiced, telling Hong: “Answer well for me—wealth and honor shared with you.
translations.idiomatic: She thrilled: “Write plainly—wealth follows.

sentences.zh: 」泓素有小才，具草，令太子自寫。

translations.literal: ” Hong always had small talent—drafted fully—ordered crown prince himself copy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong drafted; she made the prince copy.

translations.literal: Emperor examined—greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Wu read it—delighted.

sentences.zh: 先示太子少傅衛瓘，瓘大踧踖，眾人乃知瓘先有毀言，殿上皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: First showed Junior Mentor Wei Guan—Guan greatly ashamed—all knew Guan earlier had slanderous words—hall cheered ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: He flashed it at Wei Guan—Wei squirmed; courtiers jeered Guan’s prior slanders.

sentences.zh: 充密遣語妃云：「衛瓘老奴，幾破汝家。」

translations.literal: Chong secretly sent word to consort: “Old slave Wei Guan nearly ruined your house.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong whispered, “Wei Guan nearly ruined you.

translations.literal: Consort nature cruel—often personally killed several persons.
translations.idiomatic: She killed with her own hands.

sentences.zh: 或以戟擲孕妾，子隨刃墮地。

translations.literal: Sometimes threw halberd at pregnant concubine—child fell with blade to ground.
translations.idiomatic: She hurled a ji at a pregnant girl—the infant fell with the blow.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，大怒，已修金墉城，將廢之。

translations.literal: Emperor hearing greatly furious—already repaired Metal-Walled Fortress—about to depose her.
translations.idiomatic: Wu rebuilt Jinyong cage ready to depose her.

sentences.zh: 充華趙粲從容言曰：「賈妃年少，妒是婦人之情耳，長自當差。

translations.literal: Honorable Lady Zhao Can calmly said: “Consort Jia still young—jealousy is woman’s feeling—long maturity will correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Can soothed him: “She’s young—jealousy passes.

translations.literal: May Your Majesty investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Judge kindly.

sentences.zh: 」其後楊珧亦為之言曰：「陛下忘賈公閭耶？

translations.literal: ” Later Yang Zhao also spoke for her: “Your Majesty forgot Lord Jia Chong?
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao added, “Remember Jia Chong?”

translations.literal: ” Xun Xu deeply rescued her—thus avoided deposition.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Xu pleaded—she kept rank.

sentences.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇后，生河東、臨海、始平公主、哀獻皇女。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended—established empress—bore Hedong, Linhai, Shiping princesses and mournful imperial daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Hui made her queen—mother of Hedong, Linhai, Shiping princesses and others.

translations.literal: Consort violent cruelty daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Her cruelty mounted daily.

sentences.zh: 侍中賈模，后之族兄，右衛郭彰，后之從舅，並以才望居位，與楚王瑋、東安公繇分掌朝政。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Jia Mo—consort’s lineage elder; Guards-general Guo Zhang—consort’s maternal uncle—both by talent and prestige held posts sharing governance with Prince Chu Wei and Duke Dongan Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo and Guo Zhang ran court beside Sima Wei and Sima Yao.

sentences.zh: 后母廣城君養孫賈謐干預國事，權侔人主。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng raised grandson Jia Mi meddling state affairs—authority matched sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo raised Jia Mi—his power rivaled the throne.

translations.literal: Yao secretly wished depose consort—Jia faction feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao plotted deposition—Jias feared him.

sentences.zh: 及太宰亮、衛瓘等表繇徙帶方，奪楚王中候，后知瑋怨之，乃使帝作密詔令瑋誅瓘、亮，以報宿憾。

translations.literal: When Grand Mentor Liang and Wei Guan memorialized to exile Yao to Daifang and strip Prince Chu of central army inspector—consort knew Wei bore grudge—had emperor forge secret edict ordering Wei to kill Guan and Liang—settling old hatred.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Liang and Wei Guan banished Yao and clipped Wei’s guard—she forged orders for Sima Wei to murder Liang and Wei.

sentences.zh: 模知后凶暴，恐禍及己，乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢。

translations.literal: Mo knew consort fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—with Pei Yi and Wang Yan plotted deposition—Yan repented—plot slept.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo saw danger—planned coup with Pei Yi—Wang Yan backed out.

sentences.zh: 后遂荒淫放恣，與太醫令程據等亂彰內外。

translations.literal: Consort then wanton and dissolute—with Imperial Physician Cheng Ju and others licentious noise inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: She ran riot with physician Cheng Ju.

sentences.zh: 洛南有盜尉部小吏，端麗美容止，既給冢役，忽有非常衣服，眾咸疑其竊盜，尉嫌而辯之。

translations.literal: South of Luo petty clerk of thief corps—handsome bearing—assigned tomb labor yet wore extraordinary clothes—all suspected theft—captain interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: A pretty clerk toiling tombs wore silk—suspected theft.

sentences.zh: 賈后疏親欲求盜物，往聽對辭。

translations.literal: Consort distant kin sought stolen goods—went to hear interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Jia kin listened to his confession.

sentences.zh: 小吏云：「先行逢一老嫗，說家有疾病，師卜云宜得城南少年厭之，欲暫相煩，必有重報。

translations.literal: Petty clerk said: “Going ahead met old woman saying household illness—diviners said need youth south of wall to suppress—wished borrow briefly—promised rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: He met an old woman needing a southern lad to lift a curse—for pay.

sentences.zh: 於是隨去，上車下帷，內簏箱中，行可十餘里，過六七門限，開簏箱，忽見樓闕好屋。

translations.literal: Therefore followed—entered carriage hung curtains—inside bamboo chest—traveled ten-plus li—passed six-seven gates—opened chest—suddenly saw storied towers fine halls.
translations.idiomatic: She rode blindfolded through gates till palaces appeared.

sentences.zh: 問此是何處，云是天上，即以香湯見浴，好衣美食將入。

translations.literal: Asked where—said Heaven—thereupon fragrant broth bathed—fine clothes fine food led inside.
translations.idiomatic: They called it Heaven—bathed and fed him.

sentences.zh: 見一婦人，年可三十五六，短形青黑色，眉後有疵。

translations.literal: Saw one woman—age about thirty-five or six—short form blue-black—scar behind eyebrow.
translations.idiomatic: A squat dark woman in her mid-thirties bore a brow mole.

sentences.zh: 見留數夕，共寢歡宴，臨出贈此眾物。

translations.literal: Detained several nights—slept together feasting—departing gifted many goods.
translations.idiomatic: She kept him nights—sent gifts after.

sentences.zh: 」聽者聞其形狀，知是賈后，慚笑而去，尉亦解意。

translations.literal: ” Hearers hearing shape knew it was Empress Jia—left ashamed laughing—captain understood.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners recognized Jia Nanfeng—the captain dropped charges.

sentences.zh: 時他人入者多死，惟此小吏，以后愛之，得全而出。

translations.literal: Others entering mostly died—only this petty clerk—because consort loved him—escaped whole.
translations.idiomatic: Others died visiting her bed—only her pet survived.

sentences.zh: 及河東公主有疾，師巫以為宜施寬令，乃稱詔大赦天下。

translations.literal: When Hedong princess fell ill—shamans said broad edicts needed—thereupon forged edict grand amnesty realm.
translations.idiomatic: When her daughter sickened shamans demanded amnesty—she forged pardon.

sentences.zh: 初，后詐有身，內稿物為產具，遂取妹夫韓壽子慰祖養之，託諒闇所生，故弗顯。

translations.literal: At first consort feigned pregnancy—packed straw goods as birthing gear—then took sister’s husband Han Shou’s son Weizu raising—claimed mourning-hall birth—therefore not openly shown.
translations.idiomatic: She faked pregnancy—snatched Han Shou’s son Weizu—called him newborn heir.

sentences.zh: 遂謀廢太子，以所養代立。

translations.literal: Then plotted depose crown prince—establish fosterling.
translations.idiomatic: She meant to replace the heir with him.

sentences.zh: 時洛中謠曰：「南風烈烈吹黃沙，遙望魯國鬱嵯峨，前至三月滅汝家。

translations.literal: Then Luoyang rhyme said: “South wind fierce blows yellow sand—far gaze Lu kingdom towering—before third month ends your house.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang sang: “Nanfeng blasts yellow dust—Lu towers loom—by third moon your clan falls.

sentences.zh: 」后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.

sentences.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。

translations.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.

sentences.zh: 及廣城君病篤，占術謂不宜封廣城，乃改封宜城。

translations.literal: When Lady Guangcheng gravely ill—divination said unsuitable enfeoff Guangcheng—thereupon changed enfeoff Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ill diviners forbade “Guangcheng”—she became Princess Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮。

translations.literal: Consort attended illness ten-plus days—crown prince often visited Yicheng mansion—brought physicians—obedient exhaustive ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Minhuai nursed her mother—deferential.

sentences.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。

translations.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.
translations.idiomatic: She warned against Zhao Can and Jia Wu.

sentences.zh: 」后不能遵之，遂專制天下，威服內外。

translations.literal: ” Consort could not obey—thereupon monopolized realm—awe subdued inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia ignored—ruled alone.

sentences.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。

translations.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.
translations.idiomatic: She schemed with them against Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 初，誅楊駿及汝南王亮、太保衛瓘、楚王瑋等，皆臨機專斷，宦人董猛參預其事。

translations.literal: At first executing Yang Jun and Prince Runan Liang, Grand Tutor Wei Guan, Prince Chu Wei—all improvised executions—eunuch Dong Meng participated.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun, Sima Liang, Wei Guan, Sima Wei died by her whim—with eunuch Dong Meng.

sentences.zh: 猛，武帝時為寺人監，侍東宮，得親信于后，預誅楊駿，封武安侯，猛三兄皆為亭侯，天下咸怨。

translations.literal: Meng—Wu-era Inner Palace Overseer—served Eastern Palace—won consort trust—participated executing Yang Jun—enfeoffed Marquis Wu’an—Meng three elder brothers all village marquis—all realm resented.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Meng gained titles—his brothers too—the realm cursed them.

sentences.zh: 及太子廢黜，趙王倫、孫秀等因眾怨謀欲廢后[8]。

translations.literal: When crown prince deposed—Prince Zhao Lun and Sun Xiu exploiting resentment plotted depose consort [8].
translations.idiomatic: Once Minhuai fell Sima Lun and Sun Xiu used hatred to target her [8].

sentences.zh: 后數遣宮婢微服於人間視聽，其謀頗泄。

translations.literal: Consort repeatedly sent palace maids plain clothes among folk spy listen—plot leaked somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: She spied on rumors—some leaked.

sentences.zh: 后甚懼，遂害太子，以絕眾望。

translations.literal: Consort greatly afraid—thereupon harmed crown prince—cutting off hopes.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified she murdered Minhuai.

sentences.zh: 趙王倫乃率兵入宮，使翊軍校尉齊王冏入殿廢后。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Lun then led troops palace—ordered Colonel Qi Wang Jiong enter hall depose consort.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun stormed in—sent Sima Jiong to drag her out.

sentences.zh: 后與冏母有隙，故倫使之。

translations.literal: Consort with Jiong’s mother bore grudge—therefore Lun sent him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong hated her mother—Lun used him.

translations.literal: Consort alarmed said: “Why have you come!
translations.idiomatic: She cried, “Why you!”

translations.literal: ” Jiong said: “There is edict arresting consort.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong said, “Orders to seize you.

translations.literal: ” Consort said: “Edicts issue from me—what edict?
translations.idiomatic: She snapped, “Only I issue edicts.

sentences.zh: 」后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。

translations.literal: ” Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.
translations.idiomatic: She yelled at Hui—depose your wife, doom yourself.

translations.literal: ” Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?
translations.idiomatic: She asked who plotted.

translations.literal: ” Jiong said: “Liang and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: “Liang and Zhao.”

sentences.zh: 」后曰：「繫狗當繫頸，今反繫其尾，何得不然！

translations.literal: ” Consort said: “Leash dog by throat—now leash tail—how can it not be so!
translations.idiomatic: “Chain a dog by the throat—you seized the tail—no wonder!”

sentences.zh: 」至宮西，見謐尸，再舉聲而哭遽止。

translations.literal: ” Reaching palace west saw Mi corpse—raised voice twice weeping suddenly stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Jia Mi’s corpse she wailed twice—then silence.

sentences.zh: 倫乃矯詔遣尚書劉弘等持節齎金屑酒賜后死。

translations.literal: Lun then forged edict dispatch Minister Liu Hong bearing tally deliver gold-filings wine grant consort death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Lun sent Liu Hong with golden liquor.

translations.literal: Consort held rank eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven years queen.

sentences.zh: 趙粲、賈午、韓壽、董猛等皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Zhao Can, Jia Wu, Han Shou, Dong Meng executed.
translations.idiomatic: Her cabal died with her.

sentences.zh: 臨海公主先封清河，洛陽之亂，為人所略，傳賣吳興錢溫。

translations.literal: Linhai princess first enfeoffed Qinghe—Luoyang turmoil—seized by men—sold onward to Qian Wen of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Qinghe—later Linhai—was kidnapped in chaos and sold to Qian Wen.

translations.literal: Wen gave her as bride—daughter met mistress extremely cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Wen delivered her as a bride—the girl met a vicious mistress.

sentences.zh: 元帝鎮建鄴，主詣縣自言。

translations.literal: When Yuan-di governed Jianye—princess went to county explaining herself.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yuan of Jin ruled Jianye she appealed at the yamen.

sentences.zh: 元帝誅溫及女，改封臨海，宗正曹統尚之。

translations.literal: Yuan-di executed Wen and daughter—changed enfeoffment Linhai—Director of Imperial Clan Cao Tong married her.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Wen and his daughter, restored her Linhai title, and married her to Cao Tong.

translations.literal: Empress Yang of Emperor Hui
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang of Emperor Hui

sentences.zh: 惠羊皇后諱獻容，泰山南城人。

translations.literal: Empress Yang of Hui, taboo Xianrong, native of Nancheng in Taishan.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Yang Xianrong came from Nancheng in Taishan.

sentences.zh: 祖瑾，父玄之，並見外戚傳。

translations.literal: Grandfather Jin; father Xuanzhi—both treated in Outer Kin treatise.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Yang Jin and father Yang Xuanzhi appear among outer kin.

translations.literal: After Empress Jia deposed—Sun Xiu debated establishing empress.
translations.idiomatic: After Jia Nanfeng fell Sun Xiu debated a new queen.

sentences.zh: 后外祖孫旂與秀合族，又諸子自結於秀，故以太安元年立為皇后[9]。

translations.literal: Consort maternal grandfather Sun Qi shared clan with Xiu—sons bonded with Xiu—therefore first Taian year established empress [9].
translations.idiomatic: Sun Qi’s tie to Sun Xiu won her the throne in 302 [9].

translations.literal: About to enter palace—fire appeared within robes.
translations.idiomatic: Fire sparked inside her robes on palace entry.

sentences.zh: 成都王穎伐長沙王乂，以討玄之為名。

translations.literal: Prince Chengdu Ying attacked Prince Changsha Yi—using punishing Xuanzhi as pretext.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying struck Sima Yi citing Yang Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 乂敗，穎奏廢后為庶人，處金墉城。

translations.literal: Yi defeated—Ying memorialized deposing consort as commoner—housed Metal-Walled Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: After Yi fell Ying reduced her to commoner at Jinyong.

sentences.zh: 陳眕等唱伐成都王，大赦，復后位。

translations.literal: Chen Zhen and others urged attacking Chengdu prince—grand amnesty—restored consort rank.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhen’s coalition restored her with amnesty.

translations.literal: Zhang Fang entered Luoyang—again deposed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang returned and struck her title.

sentences.zh: 方逼遷大駕幸長安，留臺復后位。

translations.literal: Fang forced moving great carriage to Chang’an—Luoyang remnant court restored consort.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang dragged the court west—Luoyang ministers restored her.

translations.literal: Early Yongxing—Zhang Fang again deposed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Early Yongxing Zhang Fang deposed her again.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒矯詔，以后屢為姦人所立，遣尚書田淑敕留臺賜后死。

translations.literal: Prince Hejian Yong forged edict—because consort repeatedly installed by villains—dispatched Minister Tian Shu ordering remnant court grant consort death.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong forged orders—blaming meddlers—sent Tian Shu to kill her.

sentences.zh: 詔書累至，司隸校尉劉暾與尚書僕射荀藩、河南尹周馥馳上奏曰：「奉被手詔，伏讀惶悴。

translations.literal: Edicts piled—Metropolitan Commandant Liu Tun with Minister Director Xun Fan and Henan Intendant Zhou Fu galloped memorial saying: “Receiving handwritten edict—reading we tremble.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tun, Xun Fan, and Zhou Fu raced a plea: “Your sealed orders leave us shaking.

sentences.zh: 臣按古今書籍，亡國破家，毀喪宗祊，皆由犯眾違人之所致也。

translations.literal: Your servants examine ancient and modern writings—states ruined, houses destroyed, ancestral temples smashed—all arise from offending masses and violating men.
translations.idiomatic: History shows ruin follows when rulers betray the people.

sentences.zh: 陛下遷幸，舊京廓然，眾庶悠悠，罔所依倚。

translations.literal: Your Majesty moved west—old capital empty—multitudes drift—nothing to lean on.
translations.idiomatic: You moved west—Luoyang lies bare—the people wander homeless.

sentences.zh: 家有跂踵之心，人想鑾輿之聲，思望大德，釋兵歸農。

translations.literal: Households feel standing-on-tiptoe hearts—people imagine carriage bells—longing for great virtue—lay down arms return farming.
translations.idiomatic: Every hearth cranes for your bells—the realm wants peace and fields.

sentences.zh: 而兵纏不解，處處互起，豈非善者不至，人情猜隔故耶！

translations.literal: Yet armies tangle unresolved—everywhere mutual rising—is it not because goodness has not arrived—human hearts suspiciously blocked?
translations.idiomatic: War still spreads because trust never came.

sentences.zh: 今上官巳犯闕稱兵，焚燒宮省，百姓諠駭，宜鎮之以靜。

translations.literal: Now Shangguan Si violates palace raising troops—burning palace offices—common folk clamor—should calm with stillness.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguan Si burns the palace—calm needs quiet rule.

sentences.zh: 而大使卒至，赫然執藥，當詣金墉，內外震動，謂非聖意。

translations.literal: Yet great envoy suddenly arrives—awefully clutching poison—about to reach Metal-Walled Fortress—inner and outer shaken—say this cannot be sagely intent.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly envoys bear poison for Jinyong—none believe it is your wish.

sentences.zh: 羊庶人門戶殘破，廢放空宮，門禁峻密，若絕天地，無緣得與姦人搆亂。

translations.literal: Lady Yang commoner gate shattered—cast aside empty palace—gate guards stern dense—as if heaven severed earth—no chance conspire with villains.
translations.idiomatic: Yang wallows locked away—no traitor access.

sentences.zh: 眾無智愚，皆謂不然，刑書猥至，罪不值辜，人心一憤，易致興動。

translations.literal: Crowds wise or foolish—none deem it right—punishment writs pile—crime does not match guilt—one surge of rage—easily stirs revolt.
translations.idiomatic: No one thinks her guilty—rash execution invites riot.

sentences.zh: 夫殺一人而天下喜悅者，宗廟社稷之福也。

translations.literal: To kill one yet realm rejoices—is fortune of ancestral temple altars.
translations.idiomatic: Execute one villain and the realm cheers—that aids the shrines.

sentences.zh: 今殺一枯窮之人而令天下傷慘，臣懼凶豎乘間，妄生變故。

translations.literal: Now kill one withered poor person yet order realm mourn—your servant fears vicious youths seize gap—recklessly breed change.
translations.idiomatic: Kill a helpless widow and horrify the realm—rebels will exploit it.

sentences.zh: 臣忝司京輦，觀察眾心，實以深憂，宜當含忍。

translations.literal: Your servant humbly supervises capital region—observing crowds’ hearts—truly deeply anxious—should tolerate endure.
translations.idiomatic: We guard the capital—we plead restraint.

translations.literal: Unable bear what seen—respectfully secret memorial heard.
translations.idiomatic: We cannot stay silent.

sentences.zh: 願陛下更深與太宰參詳，勿令遠近疑惑，取謗天下。

translations.literal: Wish Your Majesty deeper consult Grand Mentor—do not let far near doubt—invite slander realm-wide.
translations.idiomatic: Consult your ministers—do not scandalize the world.

sentences.zh: 」顒見表大怒，乃遣陳顏、呂朗東收暾。

translations.literal: ” Yong seeing memorial furious—thereupon dispatched Chen Yan and Lu Lang east seize Tun.
translations.idiomatic: Yong raged—sent Chen Yan and Lu Lang to arrest Liu Tun.

translations.literal: Tun fled Qingzhou—consort thereby escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Tun fled to Qingzhou—she survived.

translations.literal: Emperor returned Luoyang—welcomed consort restored rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned he restored her.

translations.literal: Later Luoyang Magistrate He Qiao again deposed consort.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrate He Qiao struck her title again.

sentences.zh: 及張方首至，其日復后位。

translations.literal: When Zhang Fang’s head arrived—that day restored consort rank.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang’s head reached Luoyang—she rose again that day.

sentences.zh: 會帝崩，后慮太弟立為嫂叔，不得稱太后，催前太子清河王覃入，將立之，不果。

translations.literal: Meeting emperor died—consort feared younger imperial brother enthroned would make aunt-and-uncle relation—unable title empress dowager—hurried former crown prince Qinghe prince Tan enter—about establish—did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: At Hui’s death she feared Sima Chi would make her sister-in-law—she rushed Tan—failed.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，尊后為惠帝皇后，居弘訓宮。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended—honored consort as Emperor Hui’s empress—dwelling Hongxun Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huai styled her Hui’s widow at Hongxun.

translations.literal: Luoyang fell—submerged by Liu Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang fell—Liu Yao seized her.

translations.literal: Yao usurped throne—made her empress.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao made her consort.

sentences.zh: 因問曰：「吾何如司馬家兒？

translations.literal: Therefore asked: “How compare to Sima house boy?
translations.idiomatic: He asked, “How do I compare to that Sima?”

translations.literal: ” Consort said: “How may they be spoken together?
translations.idiomatic: She answered, “There is no comparison.

sentences.zh: 陛下開基之聖主，彼亡國之暗夫，有一婦一子及身三耳，不能庇之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty founding sacred lord—that defeated-house dull husband—with one wife one son and himself only three—could not shelter them.
translations.idiomatic: You are a founding hero—he could not shield wife, son, self.

sentences.zh: 貴為帝王，而妻子辱于凡庶之手。

translations.literal: Noble yet emperor—wife and children humiliated by common hands.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor though he was—kin suffered common abuse.

sentences.zh: 遣妾爾時實不思生，何圖復有今日。

translations.literal: Banished concubine then truly wished not live—how scheme again have today.
translations.idiomatic: I thought life over—never dreamed of this dawn.

sentences.zh: 妾生於高門，常謂世間男子皆然。

translations.literal: Concubine born high gate—always thought world’s men all thus.
translations.idiomatic: Raised noble—I assumed every man so weak.

sentences.zh: 自奉巾櫛以來，始知天下有丈夫耳。

translations.literal: Since serving towel comb—begin know world has real husbands.
translations.idiomatic: Since serving you I learned what men can be.

sentences.zh: 」曜甚愛寵之，生曜二子而死，偽諡獻文皇后。

translations.literal: ” Yao greatly loved favored her—bore Yao two sons then died—false posthumous title Offered Culture Empress.
translations.idiomatic: He adored her—she bore two sons then died—honored posthumously as Empress Xianwen.

translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie

translations.literal: Lady Xie named Jiu.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xie Jiu bore that name.

sentences.zh: 家本貧賤，父以屠羊為業。

translations.literal: House originally poor low—father by slaughtering sheep practiced craft.
translations.idiomatic: Her father butchered sheep.

sentences.zh: 玖清惠貞正而有淑姿，選入後庭為才人。

translations.literal: Jiu pure kind chaste upright possessing virtuous grace—selected rear chambers became talented lady.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and lovely—she entered as a talented lady.

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui in Eastern Palace—about to take consort.
translations.idiomatic: While Hui was heir they chose a princess.

sentences.zh: 武帝慮太子尚幼，未知帷房之事，乃遣往東宮侍寢，由是得幸有身。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu worried crown prince still young—did not know inner chamber affairs—therefor dispatched go Eastern Palace attend bedding—thereby gained favor pregnant.
translations.idiomatic: Wu sent her to tutor him in bed—she conceived.

sentences.zh: 賈后妒忌之，玖求還西宮，遂生愍懷太子，年三四歲，惠帝不知也。

translations.literal: Empress Jia jealous—Jiu begged return western palace—thereby bore Crown Prince Minhuai—age three four years—Emperor Hui did not know.
translations.idiomatic: Jia drove her west—she bore Minhuai—Hui knew nothing for years.

sentences.zh: 入朝，見愍懷與諸皇子共戲，執其手，武帝曰：「是汝兒也。

translations.literal: Entering court seeing Minhuai playing with imperial sons—grasped his hand—Emperor Wu said: “This is your son.
translations.idiomatic: At court Wu pointed—this is your boy.

translations.literal: ” When established crown prince—invested Jiu as Shuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Minhuai became heir she became Shuyuan.

sentences.zh: 賈后不聽太子與玖相見，處之一室。

translations.literal: Empress Jia did not permit crown prince meet Jiu—housed one chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Jia barred visits—penned mother and son apart.

sentences.zh: 及愍懷遇酷，玖亦被害焉。

translations.literal: When Minhuai met cruel fate—Jiu also murdered.
translations.idiomatic: When Minhuai died killers took her too.

sentences.zh: 永康初，詔改葬太子，因贈玖夫人印綬，葬顯平陵。

translations.literal: Early Yongkang—edict reburied crown prince—thereupon granted Jiu lady seals—buried Xianping Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Yongkang reburied Minhuai—honored her at Xianping.

translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang of Emperor Huai

sentences.zh: 懷王皇太后諱媛姬，不知所出。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Wang of Huai taboo Yuanji—birth unknown.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Wang Yuanji—parentage unknown.

sentences.zh: 初入武帝宮，拜中才人，早卒。

translations.literal: First entered Emperor Wu palace—invested Mid-ranked Talented Lady—died early.
translations.idiomatic: She entered Wu’s harem as mid-ranked talented lady—died young.

sentences.zh: 懷帝即位，追尊曰皇太后。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai ascended—posthumously honored Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Huai raised her posthumously to dowager.

translations.literal: Grand Consort Xiahou of Yuan
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiahou the Honored Consort of Yuan

sentences.zh: 元夏侯太妃名光姬，沛國譙人也。

translations.literal: Grand Consort Xiahou named Guangji—native of Qiao in Pei.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Xiahou Guangji came from Qiao in Pei.

translations.literal: Grandfather Wei—Yanzhou Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Her grandfather Xiahou Wei governed Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父莊，字仲容，淮南太守、清明亭侯。

translations.literal: Father Zhuang courtesy Zhongrong—Huainan governor Marquis Qingming Village.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Xiahou Zhuang—Huainan governor—Marquis of Qingming.

translations.literal: Consort born splendid clan—childhood bright intelligent.
translations.idiomatic: Noble blood—bright even as a girl.

sentences.zh: 琅邪武王為世子覲納焉，生元帝。

translations.literal: Prince Langya Wu as heir apparent Jin married her—bore Yuan-di.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Sima Zhou wed her for his heir—she bore Sima Rui.

sentences.zh: 及恭王薨，元帝嗣立，稱王太妃。

translations.literal: When Duke Gong died—Yuan-di succeeded—styled Wang Grand Consort.
translations.idiomatic: After Gong died Rui styled her royal dowager.

sentences.zh: 永嘉元年，薨于江左，葬琅邪國。

translations.literal: First Yongjia year died south of Yangtze—buried Langya state.
translations.idiomatic: She died in 307 south of the river—buried in Langya.

sentences.zh: 初有讖云「銅馬入海建鄴期」，太妃小字銅環，而元帝中興於江左焉。

translations.literal: At first prophecy said “bronze horse enters sea Jianye term”—grand consort childhood name Bronze Ring—and Yuan-di revived east of Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Prophecy called “bronze horse” to sea—her pet name was Bronze Ring—and Rui restored Jin south.
